taxonomic_note: Legacy Master Plant Pool name Chamaesyce fendleri is normalized to the current accepted Euphorbia name.
look_here_first: Low spreading perennial sandmat with small opposite leaves and inconspicuous axillary cyathia, usually on dry open ground.

project_inclusion.range_basis: Hays-local legacy Chamaesyce source; current Kew explicitly treats Chamaesyce fendleri as a synonym of Euphorbia fendleri.
project_inclusion.range_guardrail: Installed for active visual learning; broader exact-county reconciliation deferred.

morphology_keys.family_pattern: Euphorbiaceae/Euphorbia: milky latex and highly reduced flowers grouped into a cyathium; in sandmat spurges, opposite leaves, stem habit, hairiness, and capsule traits are especially useful.
best_field_traits: dry open sandy or rocky habitat
more substantial perennial base than tiny annual sandmats
morphology_keys.comparison_training: Think perennial low sandmat. It is generally coarser and more persistent than E. serpens and less hairy than E. villifera.
